name: Women-Oriented Street Safety in Guangzhou
description: Method replication: same task, scale and design as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (106 new Baidu street views from random points in central Guangzhou, captured 2017–2022). Original study: Cui, Gong, Yang, Zhang, Huang, Shen, Wei & Chen (2023), Buildings 13(3): 715, doi:10.3390/buildings13030715. 50 students and staff from Guangzhou and Shenzhen scored 2,377 Baidu street views of seven Guangzhou districts for perceived safety from 0 to 100, with 60 as the threshold below which a street counts as unsafe. Volunteers were in three groups: 20 women, a mixed group of 10 women and 10 men, and a hypothesis group of 10 men who scored as they thought women would feel; the women's scores were then used to map safety on walking routes between home and mass transit. Differences from the original study: (1) each participant scores 60 photos drawn at random from 106, instead of about 500 photos each with the scoring tool of Yao et al., and volunteers do not first browse all photos; (2) groups are formed on the page: women rate as themselves, and men are randomly split between rating as themselves and imagining a woman's view, so the hypothesis group is not a fixed set of 10; (3) the score is given with a 0–100 slider; (4) the mobile-phone pedestrian-flow and transit analyses are not part of the survey.
author: Cui et al.
